properties.name: A refuted finding stops reading as current: closure becomes one graph-aware computation, and both read surfaces go through it
properties.rationale:
The occasion was an agent being misled by the design's own memory. It searched during a brainstorm, met a finding another record had refuted a week earlier, saw no marker of any kind, and re-derived a settled conclusion - then reported to the owner that a detector had a sixteen-day gap. Both claims were wrong, and the measurement that showed it is what found the real defect: the detector reads the INVALIDATES edge and had been correctly silent all along.

So the fix is not where the agent first said it was. Widening the detector's fact_type filter, which is what it proposed and was asked to build, would have changed nothing here. The cause is that closure had two available answers and the two surfaces each read a different one, which is why the correction is a shared computation rather than a second filter.

WHY THE READ SURFACE IS THE WORSE HALF TO GET WRONG, and the reason this was worth stopping for: a detector reports at a boundary, to somebody who ran it. A search result is met first, in the middle of thinking about something else, and a record returned with no marker is believed. The failure is not a missed alert; it is a confident wrong belief formed from the design's own record - the exact thing reflow2 exists to prevent.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
`ClaimAge` gains `superseded_by`, and `DesignGraph::claim_age_of` is the one computation that fills it. search_design and topic_report both call it; the property-only `claim_age` remains for callers that genuinely have no graph, and returns None for the new field rather than guessing.

KEPT DISTINCT FROM `expired`, deliberately. A claim that ran out on its own terms is not a claim something refuted, and a reader needs to tell them apart. The field carries the invalidating record's ID rather than a boolean, because a reader told their source was overturned needs to be able to go and read what overturned it. Where several records invalidate one finding, the first by id is named so the answer is stable across runs rather than dependent on edge ordering.

FAILING FIRST, OBSERVED: crates/reflow2-core/tests/a_superseded_finding_does_not_read_as_current.rs was written before the field existed. It failed on the missing field, then on three real assertions once the fixture was corrected. All three pass now. It pins the CLASS - that both surfaces agree, and that the two kinds of closure stay distinguishable - rather than the one fact that exposed it.

INCIDENTAL, AND IT CONFIRMS AN OPEN FINDING: the test fixture was refused because Component requires `purpose`, which is one of the properties no constructor can set (fact:six-constructors-cannot-write-any-prose...). A type demanding a field its own constructor cannot write is the same class, one step further along.
